A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 34-page versions of the same work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison. Appendix pages 15–34 match exactly in extracted text and rendering.

before.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 and Appendices B–D report original graph heat-diffusion, mesh-PDE, and weather-forecasting evaluations, including numerical results and ablations.

after.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 and Appendices B–D retain original model evaluations on graph diffusion, mesh PDEs, and weather forecasting, with quantitative and qualitative outcomes.

M1.justification: The Taylor-truncation and compositional relaxation procedures, zero padding, unitary layers, readout networks, activations, and mesh weighting remain unchanged. Replacing 'layer/component' with 'block' in Section 5 changes terminology only.

E1.justification: Both evaluate grid-graph heat diffusion, heat/wave/Cahn-Hilliard dynamics on PyVista meshes, and ERA5 temperature and geopotential forecasting through WeatherBench2. Appendix datasets and test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments: GCN and Lie-unitary models in Table 1, the seven baselines in Table 2, MeshGraphNet in Table 5, and the weather models in Tables 13–14.

E3.justification: Data splits, initial-condition counts, input histories, rollout procedures, metrics, model budgets, and training limits are unchanged in Section 6 and Appendices B–D. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Both retain the Taylor-truncation sensitivity study, qualitative diagnostics, multiscale and local smoothness analyses, and ablations of convolution type, padding, activation, and readout dimensions in Appendices B–C.

E5.justification: Reporting practices remain identical, including best-of-five runs in Table 1, ten-run averages in Figure 8, ensemble curves, and standard deviations over test meshes and initializations. No uncertainty procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, plotted curves, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, R-UNIMESH retains heat NRMSE 51.9 ± 3.6 in Table 2. All appendix result tables and figures also match.

T1.justification: The Rayleigh-quotient definitions, approximation-error theorem, mesh-convolution corollary, assumptions, and Appendix A proofs and derivations are unchanged. Definition 2 and its explanatory footnote already appear in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unitary approximation limits, relaxed convolutions, extension to meshes, and performance on diffusive dynamics. The abstract's changed resource link does not alter these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning smoothness and geometric biases are retained, along with qualifications about mixed wave/Cahn-Hilliard performance, reduced-scale weather experiments, and the information needed to compute the theoretical bound. Appendix explanations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a direct code-repository link with a project-page link. Existing repository links and implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and compute disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish any change in external resource availability.

R1.justification: Cited-work membership and related-work positioning are unchanged. Shao et al. (2024) remains the same cited work despite corruption of its reference URL in v3.

P1.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 standardize 'block' terminology for P and B. Small punctuation and grammar edits accompany replacement of the preprint notice with an ICML 2026 proceedings notice. The narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 4 to page 5, surrounding text reflows, and the page-3 footnote is consolidated. Figure and table content is retained. The corrupted Shao reference occupies additional lines and shifts subsequent references.

improvement.justification: Although block terminology and footnote placement are slightly clearer, v3 introduces repeated 'TAG-DSSubmissionInstructions' text into both the displayed Shao et al. (2024) URL and its hyperlink target on page 13, impairing citation usability. With scientific content and appendices unchanged, this is a limited editorial decline.
